title: James P. Johnson at Carnegie Hall and Fats Domino at the Dew Drop
summary: He had never met James P. Johnson before the Carnegie concert but later recorded with him; he worked with Fats Domino in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Mmmmmnnn. On that Carnegie Hall Concert in New York, James P. Johnson was on that concert, wasn't he?
Had you ever heard him before?
No, I hadn't never met him before.
Only one I know was Pete Johnson.
Didn't you eventually then record with James P. Johnson?
Yeah. I made some records with him, too.
And you mentioned off the tape Fats Domino... having worked with him or something some place. I don't think you had mentioned that on the tape, have you?
Yeah, I worked with Fats Domino down in New Orleans...in the Dew Drop.
